content: The Principal-Agent Alignment Problem in Artificial Intelligence | EECS at UC Berkeley The Principal-Agent Alignment Problem in Artificial Intelligence Dylan Hadfield-Menell EECS Department, University of California, Berkeley Technical Report No. UCB/EECS-2021-207 August 26, 2021 http://www2.eecs.berkeley.edu/Pubs/TechRpts/2021/EECS-2021-207.pdf The field of artificial intelligence has seen serious progress in recent years, and has also caused seriousÂ concernsÂ thatÂ rangeÂ fromÂ theÂ immediateÂ harmsÂ causedÂ byÂ systemsÂ thatÂ replicate harmful biases to the more distant worry that effective goal-directed systems may, at a certain level of performance,Â be able to subvert meaningful control efforts.Â In this dissertation,Â I argue the following thesis: 1.Â TheÂ useÂ ofÂ incompleteÂ orÂ incorrectÂ incentivesÂ toÂ specifyÂ theÂ targetÂ behaviorÂ forÂ an autonomousÂ systemÂ createsÂ a valueÂ alignmentÂ problem betweenÂ theÂ principal(s),Â on whose behalf a system acts, and the system itself; 2.Â This value alignment problem can be approached in theory and practice through the development of systems that are responsive to uncertainty about the principalâs true, unobserved, intended goal; and 3.Â Value alignment problems can be modeled as a class of cooperative assistance games, which are computationally similar to the class of partially-observable Markov decision processes.Â This model captures the principalâs capacity to behave strategically in coordination with the autonomous system.Â It leads to distinct solutions to alignment problems, comparedÂ withÂ moreÂ traditionalÂ approachesÂ toÂ preferenceÂ learningÂ likeÂ inverse reinforcement learning, and demonstrates the need for strategically robust alignment solutions.
